text: Attempt 13: attempt 12's start (best ever) with a new money model: a tax controller sets each zone's rate from its demand (up to 12%), power/water built at 30% spare from cash, a second road link on the east edge for shops, dense homes from district 6.
Loan #1 ($10,000). Taxes 4/4/3; the tax controller takes over at 3,000 people.
Day one ($15,764, plan a11-day1). Build check and audit passed.

Attempt 12 stalled at ~21,000: about $2.90 spent per person against ~$0.10 per person per year of tax. Attempt 13 tests the income side first: rates that rise whenever a demand bar is pinned at maximum.
Loan #2 ($10,000), allowed in Jan 2002. Note: the game ran Jan -> Jul 2002 while the loan dialog was open.
Blocks 3 + 4 ($7,647) and coal plant #2 + 5 pumps ($4,614), plans a12-2003 and a12-power1.

Seaport + 19 north pumps ($6,046), east shops block ($2,196), second neighbor road link on the EAST edge ($1,060: 'Ashland'). Audit caught the east block unpowered (its feed assumed built factories); joined power columns x109/x116 along y56.
District 5 + west factory strip (plan a12-district5; the run was cut off by a time limit and re-run to finish). Cash could not cover its coal plant, so a gas plant ($2,000) went in its place.
District 6 with DENSE homes (test). The zoo did not fit the cash ($2,496 left, zoo $3,000): it goes in as soon as cash allows, before 15,000 people. Pipe joint at (108,65).
Loan #6 ($10,000). Ordinances on (+$308/yr). Tax controller now raises a rate at demand >= 1000 (was 1800): budget was -$818/yr with homes at 6%.
Coal plant #5 at (68,52) and the zoo ($7,024).

Dec 2006: 17,790 people, the best of any attempt at this date. The loans-vs-tax problem is back (-$818/yr); this time taxes are allowed to climb whenever demand is clearly positive, to test whether income can catch up.

Rail link + road link off the SOUTH edge ($3,609), 6 south riverbank pumps ($978). Audit caught the pumps unpowered (their line column belonged to a block not built in this attempt); line x85 extended across road y97.

Jul 2008: third attempt in a row stuck near 20,000 with factory demand at max, empty factory land and rising unemployment. The designers' book says trade capacity has to grow with the amount of industry (rail/highway links, seaports). Testing it with a south rail + road link; if factories fill, the next strategy builds links early.
